events.title: Gemini 1.5 Pro ships 1M-token context
events.summary: Google previewed Gemini 1.5 Pro, a mixture-of-experts model with a 1M-token context window.
events.significance: Interpretation: made long context a competitive axis and weakened the assumption that retrieval pipelines were the only way to ground models in large corpora.

events.title: OpenAI previews Sora text-to-video
events.summary: OpenAI previewed Sora, a diffusion-transformer video model producing minute-long clips; public release came in December 2024.
events.significance: Interpretation: extended the 'scale the transformer' thesis to video and fed the 'world simulator' framing.

events.title: Claude 3 family ends GPT-4's solo lead
events.summary: Anthropic released Claude 3 (Haiku/Sonnet/Opus), followed by Claude 3.5 Sonnet on 2024-06-20.
events.significance: Interpretation: the frontier became a multi-lab race, undercutting the belief that a single lab's lead was durable.

events.title: License-and-hire deals absorb Inflection and Character.AI
events.summary: Microsoft hired Inflection's leadership with a ~$650M licensing payment (Mar 2024); Google did a ~$2.7B license-and-rehire of Character.AI's founders (Aug 2024).
events.significance: Interpretation: signalled that independent second-tier model labs struggled to fund frontier training and that talent, not companies, was the asset being bought.

events.title: Amazon buys nuclear-adjacent data center campus from Talen
events.summary: Amazon acquired Talen Energy's data center campus next to the Susquehanna nuclear plant (~$650M).
events.significance: Interpretation: first clear sign that hyperscalers would co-locate with firm (nuclear) generation to secure AI power.

events.title: GPT-4o: native multimodal flagship made free
events.summary: OpenAI launched GPT-4o, a natively multimodal model, free in ChatGPT and at half GPT-4 Turbo's API price.
events.significance: Interpretation: GPT-4-class capability became a free consumer commodity, shifting competition to distribution and price.

events.title: 'Situational Awareness' essay frames AGI-by-2027 and a compute race
events.summary: Leopold Aschenbrenner published a long essay extrapolating compute OOMs to AGI around 2027 and trillion-dollar clusters.
events.significance: Interpretation: crystallized the national-security and compute-scaling narrative later echoed in Stargate and US policy.

events.title: Sequoia's 'AI's $600B Question'
events.summary: David Cahn estimated a ~$600B gap between implied AI infrastructure spend and AI revenue.
events.significance: Interpretation: became the canonical framing of the AI-bubble debate for the next two years.

events.title: Nvidia briefly becomes the world's most valuable company
events.summary: Nvidia's market cap passed ~$3.3T, briefly overtaking Microsoft.
events.significance: Interpretation: markets priced accelerators as the main value-capture layer of the AI stack.

events.title: Llama 3.1 405B: frontier-class open weights
events.summary: Meta released Llama 3.1 405B open weights alongside Zuckerberg's 'Open Source AI Is the Path Forward'; Llama 3 8B/70B had shipped in April.
events.significance: Interpretation: open weights near the frontier challenged the idea that model weights themselves were the moat.

events.title: GPT-4o mini prices GPT-4-class quality at $0.15/1M input tokens
events.summary: OpenAI released GPT-4o mini at $0.15/$0.60 per 1M input/output tokens, versus $30/$60 for GPT-4 at launch in March 2023.
events.significance: Interpretation: made 'LLMflation' (rapid constant-capability price decline) visible to every developer.

events.title: EU AI Act enters into force
events.summary: The AI Act entered into force with staged application dates for prohibitions (Feb 2025), GPAI duties (Aug 2025) and high-risk rules (Aug 2026, later delayed).
events.significance: Interpretation: first comprehensive horizontal AI law; set the compliance baseline that later became a target for simplification.

events.title: OpenAI o1: inference-time compute becomes a scaling axis
events.summary: OpenAI released o1-preview, trained with RL to reason in long chains of thought, with performance scaling in both RL training and test-time compute.
events.significance: Interpretation: reframed scaling from pretraining-only to RL plus test-time compute, shifting demand toward inference and opening the reasoning era.

events.title: xAI Colossus: ~100k H100s online in Memphis
events.summary: xAI announced its ~100,000-GPU Colossus cluster online after about four months of construction.
events.significance: Interpretation: showed that speed-to-power and build execution could be a competitive advantage in its own right.

events.title: Nuclear PPAs: Microsoft restarts TMI Unit 1; Google signs Kairos SMRs
events.summary: Constellation and Microsoft signed a 20-year PPA to restart TMI Unit 1 (Sept 20); Google agreed to buy up to ~500 MW from Kairos SMRs (Oct 14, 2024).
events.significance: Interpretation: AI demand began reviving retired firm generation and underwriting next-generation nuclear, making power a recognized binding constraint.

events.title: California Gov. Newsom vetoes SB 1047
events.summary: Newsom vetoed the frontier-model safety bill, citing its focus on model size rather than deployment risk.
events.significance: Interpretation: marked the limit of compute-threshold safety regulation in the US and shifted fights to transparency laws and federal preemption.

events.title: Nobel prizes to Hinton (Physics) and Hassabis/Jumper (Chemistry)
events.summary: Physics 2024 went to Hopfield and Hinton; Chemistry 2024 half to Hassabis and Jumper for AlphaFold.
events.significance: Interpretation: institutional scientific validation of deep learning and of AI-for-science.

events.title: Computer use (Oct) and Model Context Protocol (Nov) from Anthropic
events.summary: Anthropic shipped computer-use beta (Oct 22, 2024) and open-sourced MCP (Nov 25, 2024), later adopted by OpenAI (Mar 2025) and others.
events.significance: Interpretation: MCP became the de facto tool-connection standard, commoditizing integration and accelerating agents.

events.title: LBNL: data centers 4.4% of US electricity, up to 12% by 2028
events.summary: DOE/LBNL reported data centers used ~176 TWh (4.4%) of US electricity in 2023 and could reach 6.7-12% by 2028.
events.significance: Interpretation: gave policymakers an official baseline for AI-driven load growth.

events.title: o3 scores ~76-88% on ARC-AGI-1
events.summary: OpenAI previewed o3; ARC Prize verified ~75.7% (limited compute) and ~87.5% (high compute) on ARC-AGI-1.
events.significance: Interpretation: test-time compute cracked a benchmark designed to resist scaling, though at very high cost per task.

events.title: DeepSeek-R1: open-weight reasoning at a fraction of the cost
events.summary: DeepSeek released R1 under MIT license, matching o1 on many benchmarks; its V3 base reported a ~$5.6M final training run.
events.significance: Interpretation: showed RL-based reasoning could be replicated cheaply and openly, compressing frontier leads and triggering a market repricing.

events.title: Stargate: $500B US AI infrastructure pledge
events.summary: OpenAI, SoftBank, Oracle and MGX announced Stargate, intending $500B over four years ($100B immediately).
events.significance: Interpretation: moved frontier labs from renting compute to directly sponsoring GW-scale campuses.

events.title: Nvidia loses ~$589B in one day
events.summary: Nvidia fell ~17% after DeepSeek, the largest single-day market-value loss for a US company at the time.
events.significance: Interpretation: markets briefly feared efficiency would shrink compute demand (Jevons debate); demand subsequently accelerated.

events.title: Claude Code launches; coding agents become the killer app
events.summary: Anthropic launched Claude Code with Claude 3.7 Sonnet (preview) and made it GA with Claude 4 (May 22, 2025).
events.significance: Interpretation: terminal-native coding agents became the first agent category with large paid usage, reshaping revenue mix toward agentic tokens.

events.title: METR: AI task horizons double every ~7 months
events.summary: METR found frontier models' 50% task-completion horizon had doubled ~every 7 months since 2019 (Claude 3.7 Sonnet ~50 minutes).
events.significance: Interpretation: offered a single trend line for agent capability that anchored forecasts and policy discussion.

events.title: Reasoning goes mainstream: Gemini 2.5 Pro, o3, o4-mini
events.summary: Google shipped Gemini 2.5 Pro (Mar 25) as a thinking model; OpenAI released o3 and o4-mini (Apr 16) with tool use inside reasoning.
events.significance: Interpretation: reasoning became table stakes across labs and inference-time compute a standard cost driver.

events.title: H20 export licensing and the revenue-share reversal
events.summary: The US required licenses for Nvidia H20 sales to China (Apr 2025), then allowed them under a 15% revenue-share arrangement (Aug 2025); H200 sales were later allowed under license.
events.significance: Interpretation: chip export policy turned transactional, and China accelerated domestic accelerators and open models.

events.title: Claude 4 (Opus/Sonnet) targets long-running agents
events.summary: Anthropic released Claude Opus 4 and Sonnet 4, emphasizing multi-hour agentic coding; activated ASL-3 protections for Opus 4.
events.significance: Interpretation: frontier competition shifted from chat quality to sustained agentic work.

events.title: Meta buys 49% of Scale AI and forms Superintelligence Labs
events.summary: Meta invested ~$14.3B in Scale AI, hired Alexandr Wang, and launched Meta Superintelligence Labs with large talent offers.
events.significance: Interpretation: talent and data pipelines priced like strategic assets; marked Meta's pivot away from Llama-first open strategy.

events.title: Chinese open-weight wave: Qwen3, Kimi K2, DeepSeek V3.x
events.summary: Alibaba (Qwen3, Apr), Moonshot (Kimi K2, Jul) and DeepSeek (V3.1/V3.2) released strong open-weight models.
events.significance: Interpretation: China became the center of gravity for open weights as Meta retreated, keeping the open-closed gap to a few months.

events.title: US AI Action Plan
events.summary: The White House issued America's AI Action Plan prioritizing deregulation, data-center/power permitting and AI exports.
events.significance: Interpretation: US policy pivoted from safety framing (2023 EO) to build-out and competitiveness.

events.title: GPT-5 launches to mixed reception
events.summary: OpenAI released GPT-5 as a routed system at $1.25/$10 per 1M tokens.
events.significance: Interpretation: aggressive pricing and an incremental-feeling launch fed 'scaling plateau' and bubble narratives in late 2025.

events.title: MIT NANDA '95% of GenAI pilots fail' report
events.summary: MIT NANDA's 'GenAI Divide' report claimed ~95% of organizations saw zero measurable return from GenAI pilots.
events.significance: Interpretation: became a widely cited (and contested) data point in the enterprise-ROI and bubble debate.

events.title: Stanford 'Canaries in the Coal Mine' entry-level labor study
events.summary: ADP payroll analysis found ~13% relative employment decline for 22-25-year-olds in the most AI-exposed occupations.
events.significance: Interpretation: first large-sample evidence of early-career labor effects, shifting the labor debate from speculation to measurement.

events.title: OpenAI's GW-scale compute deals with Oracle, Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom
events.summary: Reported ~$300B Oracle contract, Nvidia up-to-$100B investment LOI (10 GW), AMD 6 GW with warrants, Broadcom 10 GW, AWS $38B.
events.significance: Interpretation: supplier-financed demand ('circular financing') became the core of the bubble critique.

events.title: OpenAI recapitalizes as a public benefit corporation
events.summary: OpenAI's for-profit became OpenAI Group PBC under the OpenAI Foundation; Microsoft took ~27%.
events.significance: Interpretation: removed the structural barrier to mega-fundraising and an eventual IPO.

events.title: Nvidia first company to reach $5 trillion market cap
events.summary: Nvidia closed above $5T market capitalization.
events.significance: Interpretation: peak expression of the belief that value accrues to the accelerator layer.

events.title: Gemini 3 retakes benchmark lead; Antigravity agent IDE
events.summary: Google released Gemini 3 across Search, the Gemini app and developer platforms with record benchmark claims (e.g., 37.5% HLE).
events.significance: Interpretation: shifted perception toward Google's full-stack (TPU + distribution) advantage.

events.title: Oracle CDS at highest since 2009 as AI debt fears mount
events.summary: Oracle five-year CDS hit post-2009 highs amid large bond issuance and ~$248B in data-center lease commitments.
events.significance: Interpretation: AI-bubble concern moved from equity valuations to credit markets.

events.title: Executive Order 14365 targets state AI laws
events.summary: Trump signed an EO creating a DOJ AI Litigation Task Force to challenge state AI laws and directing a federal preemption proposal.
events.significance: Interpretation: federal-vs-state jurisdiction became the central US AI governance fight.

events.title: Q1 frontier refresh: Claude Opus 4.6 and Gemini 3.1 Pro
events.summary: Aggregator timelines list Claude Opus 4.6 (Feb 5) and Gemini 3.1 Pro (Feb 19, 2026).
events.significance: Interpretation: release cadence compressed to roughly bi-monthly frontier increments.

events.title: Nvidia FY2026: $215.9B revenue, $62.3B data center quarter
events.summary: NVIDIA reported Q4 FY2026 revenue $68.1B and data center $62.3B; FY2026 revenue $215.9B (+65%).
events.significance: Interpretation: demand kept accelerating despite the DeepSeek scare and bubble debate.

events.title: Pentagon labels Anthropic a supply chain risk
events.summary: After Anthropic refused to drop restrictions on mass domestic surveillance and autonomous weapons uses, the Pentagon designated it a supply chain risk.
events.significance: Interpretation: lab usage policies became a direct point of conflict with the US government.

events.title: OpenAI raises $122B at $852B post-money
events.summary: OpenAI reportedly closed a $122B round at an $852B valuation led by SoftBank and Microsoft.
events.significance: Interpretation: private capital scale for labs reached sovereign-wealth levels.

events.title: Project Glasswing: Claude Mythos withheld for cyber-defense only
events.summary: Anthropic gave its unreleased Claude Mythos Preview to 40+ security partners to find and fix vulnerabilities instead of releasing it generally.
events.significance: Interpretation: first major case of a lab withholding a frontier model on offensive-cyber capability grounds.

events.title: Meta's first post-Llama model (Avocado series) after delays
events.summary: After delaying Avocado, Meta reportedly released Muse Spark (first Avocado-series model) in the Meta AI app, replacing Llama in its assistants.
events.significance: Interpretation: confirmed Meta's shift away from open Llama releases toward closed, product-first models.

events.title: GPT-5.5 released
events.summary: OpenAI released GPT-5.5, framed as a step toward doing work on a computer.
events.significance: Interpretation: computer-use agents became the headline capability for frontier releases.

events.title: DeepSeek V4: 1.6T open MoE with 1M context
events.summary: DeepSeek released V4-Pro (1.6T) and V4-Flash (284B) open-weight MoE previews with 1M-token context.
events.significance: Interpretation: Chinese open weights stayed within months of the frontier (Epoch: ~4-month lag in 2026).

events.title: Big-four 2026 capex guidance reaches ~$700-725B
events.summary: Q1 2026 earnings put combined Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet and Meta 2026 capex at roughly $700-725B, up ~75% from ~$410B in 2025; three of four raised guidance.
events.significance: Interpretation: capex kept rising despite bubble concerns, with analysts projecting >$1T in 2027; part of the rise is component inflation.

events.title: Anthropic Series H: $65B at $965B; $47B run-rate
events.summary: Anthropic raised $65B at a $965B post-money valuation, above OpenAI's $852B, with run-rate revenue above $47B.
events.significance: Interpretation: enterprise/agentic-coding revenue made Anthropic the highest-valued private lab, overturning the consumer-first assumption.

events.title: OpenAI confidentially files for an IPO
events.summary: OpenAI confidentially submitted a draft registration statement (reported May 22/June 8), with reports of a Q4 2026 target at $852B-$1T+.
events.significance: Interpretation: frontier labs moving to public markets would test AI valuations against disclosure.

events.title: US Commerce order leads Anthropic to cut off Mythos 5 and Fable 5
events.summary: A Commerce letter asked Anthropic to restrict Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for foreign nationals; Anthropic shut off both for all customers; Mythos 5 was partially restored to US critical-infrastructure defenders on June 27.
events.significance: Interpretation: first de facto US government recall of a deployed commercial frontier model; model access became export-controlled.

events.title: EU Digital Omnibus delays AI Act high-risk obligations
events.summary: Parliament adopted the deal delaying Annex III high-risk obligations from Aug 2, 2026 to Dec 2, 2027 and Annex I to Aug 2, 2028.
events.significance: Interpretation: Europe shifted from rule-setting toward competitiveness, mirroring the US deregulatory turn.

events.title: LBNL update: data centers 4.7% of US power in 2024, ~11.8% by 2030
events.summary: LBNL's 2025 update projected data centers at 11.8% of US electricity by 2030 (range 9.5-15.3%); secondary reporting puts 2024 use at 192 TWh (4.7%).
events.significance: Interpretation: near-term load came in below some forecasts, but the decade outlook still implies a structural power build.

events.title: Bipartisan federal AI preemption discussion draft
events.summary: Reps. Obernolte and Trahan released a draft freezing state laws on AI development for three years; it stalled by September.
events.significance: Interpretation: legislative preemption remained unresolved, leaving a patchwork of state laws.

events.title: Claude Opus 5 launches the Claude 5 family
events.summary: Anthropic released Claude Opus 5 at $5/$25 per 1M tokens with 1M context, alongside Sonnet 5 and Fable 5 tiers.
events.significance: Interpretation: frontier list prices held flat while capability rose.

events.title: Nvidia Q2 FY2027: $89B data center quarter, $108B guide
events.summary: NVIDIA reported revenue ~$96.2B and data center $89.0B (+117% y/y), guided Q3 to $108B, and said Vera Rubin was ramping.
events.significance: Interpretation: AI hardware demand was still accelerating at the research cutoff.

events.title: Lab run-rates reach ~$65-70B (Anthropic, OpenAI)
events.summary: Anthropic's run-rate reportedly topped $65B by end-July 2026 (from ~$9B at end-2025); OpenAI's reportedly neared $70B in September.
events.significance: Interpretation: if accurate, AI model revenue grew fast enough to narrow Sequoia's '$600B question' gap, though run-rates are not audited revenue.

events.title: GPT-6 'Astra' rolls out with cyber guardrails
events.summary: OpenAI rolled out GPT-6 Astra to business testers, with a cyber-guardrailed version for paid ChatGPT users; reported API price $10/$50 per 1M tokens.
events.significance: Interpretation: frontier list prices rose again for the newest tier, and cyber controls became a launch prerequisite.

events.title: Claude Opus 5.5 at lower price
events.summary: Anthropic launched Claude Opus 5.5 at $4/$20 per 1M tokens, 20% below Opus 5 on list price (the source headline says 40% cheaper, possibly on effective cost).
events.significance: Interpretation: price competition at the frontier continued alongside capability gains.

periods.label: Multimodal, open-weight and infrastructure year; reasoning arrives
periods.boundaryRationale: Starts as GPT-4 parity spreads (Gemini 1.5, Claude 3) and infrastructure/power becomes the story; ends Dec 2024 with o3/ARC-AGI. Proposed revision (interpretation): the conceptual break to the reasoning era is o1 (2024-09-12), so a research-driven split would end p2024 at 2024-08 and start p2025 at 2024-09; we keep calendar ranges for comparability but tag Sept-Dec 2024 events as the opening of the reasoning era.
periods.consensus: Scaling pretraining compute remained the dominant thesis, with frontier quality converging across OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and (open) Meta. Advantage was believed to sit in compute access and Nvidia GPUs, and power emerged as the new constraint, driving nuclear PPAs. Multimodality and long context were seen as the next product frontier; by late 2024, o1 introduced inference-time compute as a second scaling axis.

minorityViews.view: Pretraining scaling is hitting diminishing returns; new paradigms (RL/test-time compute) needed.
minorityViews.heldBy: Ilya Sutskever (NeurIPS Dec 2024 'pretraining as we know it will end'), Gary Marcus
minorityViews.laterImportance: Hindsight: partly vindicated as RL/reasoning drove 2025 gains, though pretraining scale-ups (e.g., larger 2026 models) continued.

minorityViews.view: AI capex vastly outruns revenue (the '$600B question').
minorityViews.heldBy: David Cahn (Sequoia), Goldman Sachs' Jim Covello
minorityViews.laterImportance: Hindsight: framed the 2025-26 bubble debate; reported 2026 lab run-rates (~$65-70B each) narrowed but did not close the gap.

minorityViews.view: AGI by ~2027 via compute OOMs; a national-security race with China.
minorityViews.laterImportance: Hindsight: the compute race and government involvement (Stargate, export controls, 2026 Commerce order) materialized; AGI claim unresolved.

bottlenecks.note: Allocation constrained; Nvidia captured most value.
Drove nuclear PPAs (TMI restart, Kairos, Talen).
'Data wall' discussion; synthetic data and RL as responses.
EU AI Act in force; California SB 1047 vetoed.

perceivedAdvantage: Compute scale and access to Nvidia GPUs
actualAdvantage: Interpretation (as of 2026-10-11): Nvidia's accelerator position captured the largest realized profits (data center revenue rose from $47.5B in FY2024 to $193.7B in FY2026; evidence nvda_fy, nv_q4fy26).
Interpretation: enterprise/developer focus (Anthropic's coding position seeded by Claude 3.5 Sonnet) proved more valuable than expected, per 2026 run-rates and valuation.
Interpretation: model weights were not a durable moat; open models stayed months behind (Epoch).
periods.investment: Attention centered on GPUs and data centers; Nvidia became the most valuable company in June 2024. Hyperscaler capex rose sharply in 2024 (combined total not re-sourced this session; see gaps). OpenAI's 2024 revenue was ~$3.7B (reported), far below infrastructure spend.

energy.state: Power became a recognized constraint; first nuclear PPAs for AI loads.

semis.state: Nvidia H100/H200 dominant; Blackwell announced; market cap record.

cloud.state: Hyperscaler capex ramp; 100k-GPU clusters; GPU clouds proliferate.

data.state: 'Data wall' concerns; licensing deals and synthetic data.

architecture.state: Transformers dominant; MoE and long context spread; diffusion transformers for video.

training.state: Pretraining scaling plus RL for reasoning (o1) emerges late in the year.

inference.state: Prices for GPT-4-class quality collapse (GPT-4o mini); test-time compute introduced.

models.state: Multi-lab frontier parity; open weights reach 405B.

platforms.state: APIs and early agent tooling; MCP launched in Nov.

agents.state: Computer use and o1 make agents plausible but unreliable.

apps.state: ChatGPT dominates; copilots in enterprise; early coding assistants.

distribution.state: Assistants bundled into OS/productivity suites; free GPT-4o.

economics.state: Bubble question raised; talent acquihires; labs heavily loss-making.

society.state: EU AI Act in force; SB 1047 vetoed; Nobel prizes for AI.

underestimated: Coding as the first large agent market

periods.label: Reasoning, inference scaling and coding agents; the circular-capex boom
periods.boundaryRationale: Opens with DeepSeek-R1 and Stargate (Jan 20-21, 2025), which together reframed costs and capital; closes with Gemini 3 / Opus 4.5 (Nov), Oracle credit stress and EO 14365 (Dec). Proposed revision (interpretation): the reasoning era arguably begins with o1 in Sept 2024; the agentic-coding/compute-megadeal phase could be dated from Feb 2025 (Claude Code) onward.
periods.consensus: Reasoning via RL and test-time compute became the main scaling lever, and coding agents the first clear product-market fit for agents. Efficiency shocks (DeepSeek) did not reduce demand; instead labs signed GW-scale compute deals and hyperscaler capex roughly doubled. Policy turned toward build-out and competition (AI Action Plan), while the bubble debate intensified around circular financing and enterprise ROI.

minorityViews.view: Most enterprise GenAI pilots deliver no ROI.
minorityViews.laterImportance: Hindsight: contested; 2026 enterprise run-rate growth at Anthropic/OpenAI suggests concentrated ROI in coding/agents.

minorityViews.view: Circular financing and debt-funded data centers resemble a bubble.
minorityViews.heldBy: Credit analysts; commentators citing Oracle CDS
minorityViews.laterImportance: Hindsight: no crash by 2026-10-11; capex guidance kept rising, but credit concerns persisted.

minorityViews.view: LLMs are a dead end for AGI; world models needed.
minorityViews.laterImportance: Hindsight: unresolved; LLM-based agents kept improving on METR horizons.

technologies: Claude Code, Codex and agentic IDEs
Open-weight reasoning models (R1, Qwen3, Kimi K2)
architectures: RL-trained reasoning models with tool use

bottlenecks.note: Labs contracted 10+ GW of future capacity.
H20 licensing reversals; China pushed domestic chips.
MIT NANDA 95% claim vs fast coding-agent adoption.

actualAdvantage: Interpretation (as of 2026-10-11): coding/agentic enterprise usage produced the fastest revenue growth (Anthropic run-rate ~$9B end-2025 to >$65B by July 2026, press-reported).
Interpretation: Nvidia continued to capture outsized profits (data center revenue +117% y/y in Q2 FY2027).
Interpretation: DeepSeek-style efficiency did not erode compute demand; capex roughly doubled again in 2026 guidance.
periods.investment: Big-four capex reached roughly $410B in 2025 (per 2026 reporting). OpenAI signed ~26+ GW of compute commitments across Oracle, Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom and AWS; Stargate pledged $500B. Meta invested ~$14.3B in Scale AI. Anthropic raised $13B at $183B (Sept 2025); Nvidia reached a $5T market cap (Oct 2025).

energy.state: GW-scale campuses planned; gas turbines and nuclear deals; permitting prioritized by US policy.

semis.state: Blackwell ramps; custom ASICs (TPU, Trainium, Broadcom) gain; export-control whiplash.

cloud.state: Neoclouds and Oracle become major AI hosts; multi-GW contracts.

data.state: RL environments and expert data vendors (Scale, Surge, Mercor) become strategic.

architecture.state: Sparse MoE and efficient attention spread from Chinese labs.

training.state: RL post-training scaled; reasoning distilled into smaller models.

inference.state: Reasoning tokens drive inference demand; prices per capability keep falling.

models.state: Rapid frontier releases; open weights led by Chinese labs.

platforms.state: MCP adopted across vendors; agent SDKs.

agents.state: Coding agents reach broad adoption; task horizons ~hours.

apps.state: Coding tools (Cursor, Claude Code, Codex) are the breakout category.

distribution.state: Google integrates Gemini into Search; ChatGPT scale; Meta retreats from open Llama.

economics.state: Circular financing, Oracle debt, enterprise ROI and entry-level labor debates.

society.state: US AI Action Plan; EU GPAI obligations from Aug 2025; preemption EO in Dec.

periods.label: Agentic enterprise revenue, ~$700B capex and government control of frontier access
periods.boundaryRationale: Calendar start; the research cutoff is 2026-10-11. Defining events: Pentagon-Anthropic clash (Mar), Glasswing/Mythos (Apr), ~$700B+ capex guidance (Apr), Anthropic $965B (May), Commerce order cutting off Mythos 5/Fable 5 (Jun), GPT-6 and Claude 5.x (Jul-Sep). Proposed revision (interpretation): Dec 2025 (Gemini 3/Opus 4.5 frontier, EO 14365, Oracle credit stress) could open this period, since 2026 themes continue from it.
periods.consensus: As understood during 2026 (per contemporaneous reporting): agentic coding and enterprise agents drove the fastest revenue growth in software history, with Anthropic and OpenAI reporting run-rates in the tens of billions. Hyperscaler capex guidance of ~$700B+ and accelerating Nvidia sales signalled no near-term slowdown, even as IPO plans and credit concerns tested valuations. Frontier capability, especially offensive cyber, drew direct government intervention (Pentagon designation, Commerce order), and regulation shifted toward delay (EU omnibus) and federal preemption attempts.

minorityViews.view: Run-rate revenue figures overstate durable revenue; AI infrastructure is overbuilt and debt-financed.
minorityViews.laterImportance: Unresolved at cutoff; IPO disclosures would test it.

minorityViews.view: Restricting frontier models by government order is a dangerous precedent.
minorityViews.heldBy: Anthropic (publicly disagreed with the Commerce order); critics of the Pentagon designation incl. Sen. Gillibrand

minorityViews.view: Open weights will keep pace with the frontier.
minorityViews.laterImportance: Epoch measured a ~4-month lag in 2026, slightly larger than 2025's ~3 months.

technologies: Claude Opus 4.6-4.8, Claude 5 family (Opus 5, Sonnet 5, Fable 5), Opus 5.5, Mythos (restricted)
architectures: Restricted-access frontier tiers with cyber guardrails

bottlenecks.item: Government permission to deploy frontier models
bottlenecks.note: Commerce order on Mythos 5/Fable 5; Pentagon supply-chain designation.
Nvidia supply commitments ~$279B mostly memory; Microsoft cited ~$25B component inflation.
Abilene ramping toward 1.2 GW by Q4 2026 (Epoch est.).
METR horizons above ~16h reported unreliable with current suite.
OpenAI confidential IPO filing; Anthropic IPO expected.

actualAdvantage: Not assessable with hindsight at the cutoff (2026-10-11); see gaps.
periods.investment: Big-four 2026 capex guidance ~$700-725B (vs ~$410B in 2025). OpenAI raised $122B at $852B (Mar); Anthropic $30B at $380B (Feb) then $65B at $965B (May). Nvidia data center revenue $75.2B (Q1 FY27) and $89.0B (Q2 FY27), with Q3 guide $108B total revenue.
